title: Fasciola spp. Faecal Sedimentation Protocol for Egg Concentration and DNA Isolation
author: Nichola Calvani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jw9cph6

steps.title: Prepare faecal suspension
steps.instruction: Mix 3 g (sheep) or 6 g (cattle) faecal sample with distilled water to obtain a homogeneous solution.

steps.title: Sieve and initial sedimentation
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 270 µm nylon sieve into a 250 ml conical measuring cylinder, top with distilled water, and allow sedimentation for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Second sedimentation transfer
steps.instruction: After 3 minutes aspirate the supernatant, pour the sediment into a 100 ml conical measuring cylinder, rinse the 250 ml cylinder into it, top with distilled water, and let sediment for a further 3 minutes.

steps.title: Third sedimentation transfer
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, transfer the remaining sediment into a 15 ml centrifuge tube, rinse the 100 ml cylinder into the tube, top with distilled water, and allow sedimentation for a final 3 minutes.

steps.title: Leave sediment for downstream
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant leaving 2 ml of sediment; proceed to egg counting (step 6) or go straight to DNA isolation (step 9).

steps.title: Egg counting preparation
steps.instruction: Add 2 drops of 1 % methylene blue to the sediment, shake to mix, rinse onto a 6.5 × 17 × 1 cm grid perspex tray (add distilled water if needed), examine under a stereomicroscope at 15× magnification and count yellow‑brown Fasciola eggs. For cattle, divide the count by 2 to obtain eggs per gram (EPG); sheep values are taken as observed.

steps.title: Pellet formation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 15 ml tube at 2500 g for 10 minutes to form a pellet (whether after egg counting or directly from step 5).

steps.title: Transfer pellet to bead‑beating tube
steps.instruction: Using Pasteur pipettes and fine wooden applicator sticks, move the entire pellet into a pre‑prepared bead‑beating tube containing ceramic beads and lysis buffer (BioLine Isolate Fecal DNA Kit).

steps.title: Mechanical lysis
steps.instruction: Disrupt the sample at 6.0 m s⁻¹ for 40 seconds on a FastPrep®‑24 homogeniser, then place the tube on ice until DNA isolation and amplification are continued.
